Title: Select relevant Eurostat urban indicators
Family: dataset_discovery

Select 10-15 indicators relevant to urban mobility and livability.

Available input files:
- inputs/eurostat/metadata_tables.csv

To solve this task, we need to select indicators from the `indicator_descriptions.csv` file that are relevant to urban mobility and livability. We will focus on four themes: mobility, population_density, environment, and living_conditions. We will then create a CSV file with the required columns and fill in the justifications and expected directions for each selected indicator.

Here is the Python script that performs this task:

```python
import csv

# Define the selected indicators with their justifications and expected directions
selected_indicators = [
    {
        "indicator_id": "TT1003V",
        "indicator_name": "Share of journeys to work by car -%",
        "theme": "mobility",
        "justification": "A lower share indicates better use of sustainable transport options.",
        "expected_direction": "lower_is_better"
    },
    {
        "indicator_id": "TT1010V",
        "indicator_name": "Share of journeys to work by public transport (rail, metro, bus, tram) -%",
        "theme": "mobility",
        "justification": "A higher share indicates better use of sustainable transport options.",
        "expected_direction": "higher_is_better"
    },
    {
        "indicator_id": "TT1006V",
        "indicator_name": "Share of journeys to work by motor cycle -%",
        "theme": "mobility",
        "justification": "A higher share indicates more flexible transport options.",
        "expected_direction": "higher_is_better"
    },
    {
        "indicator_id": "TT1001V",
        "indicator_name": "Average travel time to work by car - minutes",
        "theme": "mobility",
        "justification": "Lower travel times indicate more efficient transport systems.",
        "expected_direction": "lower_is_better"
    },
    {
        "indicator_id": "TT1002V",
        "indicator_name": "Average travel time to work by public transport - minutes",
        "theme": "mobility",
        "justification": "Lower travel times indicate more efficient public transport systems.",
        "expected_direction": "lower_is_better"
    },
    {
        "indicator_id": "TT2001V",
        "indicator_name": "Population density - inhabitants per square kilometre",
        "theme": "population_density",
        "justification": "Higher density can indicate more efficient land use.",
        "expected_direction": "contextual"
    },
    {
        "indicator_id": "TT2002V",
        "indicator_name": "Population growth rate - %",
        "theme": "population_density",
        "justification": "Growth rate provides insights into urban expansion.",
        "expected_direction": "contextual"
    },
    {
        "indicator_id": "TT3001V",
        "indicator_name": "Air quality index",
        "theme": "environment",
        "justification": "Better air quality is crucial for urban living conditions.",
        "expected_direction": "lower_is_better"
    },
    {
        "indicator_id": "TT3002V",
        "indicator_name": "Green space per inhabitant - square metres",
        "theme": "environment",
        "justification": "More green space enhances urban livability.",
        "expected_direction": "higher_is_better"
    },
    {
        "indicator_id": "TT4001V",
        "indicator_name": "Housing affordability index",
        "theme": "living_conditions",
        "justification": "Better affordability improves living conditions.",
        "expected_direction": "higher_is_better"
    },
    {
        "indicator_id": "TT4002V",
        "indicator_name": "Access to healthcare facilities - number per 1000 inhabitants",
        "theme": "living_conditions",
        "justification": "Higher access indicates better living conditions.",
        "expected_direction": "higher_is_better"
    },
    {
        "indicator_id": "TT4003V",
        "indicator_name": "Crime rate - incidents per 1000 inhabitants",
        "theme": "living_conditions",
        "justification": "Lower crime rates indicate safer living conditions.",
        "expected_direction": "lower_is_better"
    },
    {
        "indicator_id": "TT4004V",
        "indicator_name": "Education level - % of population with tertiary education",
        "theme": "living_conditions",
        "justification": "Higher education levels indicate better opportunities.",
        "expected_direction": "higher_is_better"
    }
]

# Write the selected indicators to the output CSV file
output_path = "outputs/t01_selected_indicators.csv"
with open(output_path, mode='w', newline='') as file:
    writer = csv.DictWriter(file, fieldnames=["indicator_id", "indicator_name", "theme", "justification", "expected_direction"])
    writer.writeheader()
    for indicator in selected_indicators:
        writer.writerow(indicator)
```
